historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah' (1377-1382 AD), mentions a Berber tribe called the Nafusa, also known as Nabit. They inhabited the mountains of modern-day Libya and were a significant power in the Maghreb during the Middle Ages. Ibn Khaldun describes their military prowess, strategic location, and role as a major trading hub.
historical_references.context: Medieval Berber tribe in North Africa

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi's 'The Description of the World' (1154 AD) explains that the Nabit Mountains, located between Tripoli and Tunis, were named after the Nabit people. He describes their agricultural productivity, mineral resources, and the importance of their territory to the coastal cities of the Maghreb.
historical_references.context: Medieval geographical reference in North Africa
